clue.text: Philosophical Society dons were in control

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the ruling verb wears the society letter inside it

parts.note: monarchs who were in control reigned

explanation.surface: A philosophical society whose academic dons held the reins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosophical' looks like part of the society's name, but it is the definition; 'dons' is a verb, not university fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone philosophical about a setback has accepted it calmly, which is being resigned to it.

clue.text: He dreads being mistaken for people like Prince Harry

indicators.note: letters that are mistaken are got wrong, so they come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A man fears being confused with the likes of the prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Harry is famously ginger-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Harry has red hair, so he is an example of people with that hair colour.

clue.text: Crushing blow cut short party

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter of the word for short is lost

parts.note: squat means short and thickset
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A devastating blow cut a party short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' reads as one phrase, but 'cut' docks SQUAT (short) to SQUA.
explanation.definitionFit: A squabash is a crushing rebuke or knockout criticism, an old word for a devastating blow.

clue.text: Colleagues single-handedly keep making ill-informed judgements

indicators.note: the words keep the answer within their letters, holding it across the join

explanation.surface: Colleagues working alone keep arriving at poorly informed decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Guessing is estimating without enough evidence, so forming opinions without full information.

clue.text: Relay broadcast ahead of time

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A relayed transmission went out before schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected or appointed moment.

clue.text: Book set in university town in Cheshire is fit for purpose

indicators.note: the book letter is placed within the town's name

parts.note: Sale is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A book whose setting is a university town in Cheshire turns out to serve its purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town near Manchester in the English county of Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable can be put to work, so it is adequate for the job it was meant for.

clue.text: Firm dropping case of security guards

indicators.note: the outer letters stand guard around the dropping
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a turd is a dropping of dung

explanation.surface: A company lets its security staff go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' looks like a verb, getting rid of guards, but it is a noun for dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and sturdy are synonyms meaning solid and strongly built.

clue.text: Act the giddy goat and get lost

definitions.meaning: to act the giddy goat is to fool about, which as wordplay is to ..., a fool
a rude order to go away

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop playing the fool and clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: To act the giddy goat is a British idiom for messing about; read as BE A TIT, a tit being a foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the phrase is slang for go away; split as three words it means be a fool.

clue.text: Opening to see recording of Small Island

indicators.note: a recording plays back the sound of the words

parts.note: an islet is a small island

explanation.surface: An opening night to see a recording of the play Small Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Small Island is a novel by Andrea Levy, also staged as a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, including one to peep through.

clue.text: Rally where Republican really embraces concern for the environment

indicators.note: the two pieces hug the green prefix between them

parts.note: very means really, as in very good
eco is short for ecological, environmental concern

explanation.surface: A political rally where a Republican really does take up green causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a political meeting; it is a recovery, as in a market rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally in prices or health is a recovery after a decline.

indicators.note: the minus sign says a numeral is subtracted from the verb before it

parts.note: to infer is to deduce
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: It reads like a scrap of arithmetic with a tennis score as its result.
explanation.walkthrough: The minus sign takes D (Roman 500) out of DEDUCE. In tennis a score of 40-40 is called deuce.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, forty all is given its own name, the tied score from which a player needs two clear points.

clue.text: European Union created reforms to change political beliefs

indicators.note: to re-form is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: The European Union created reforms aimed at altering political opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun, the reforms the Union created, but it is the anagram signal working on EU plus CREATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-educate someone is to retrain their thinking, typically to bring their politics into line.

clue.text: Government representatives backed me by detaining fool

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the two letters of 'me' are read the other way
the little word holds the fool within it

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they were supported, then held up by an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a body of envoys representing their government in a foreign capital.

clue.text: One spawned by former partner

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
a wife is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: Someone sired by an ex-partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One spawned' sounds like a child, but spawning is what fish do: the oldwife is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Several sea fish are called the oldwife, and fish hatch from spawn, so one is a creature spawned.

clue.text: Engineer gripped by depression stopped working outside and became detached

indicators.note: the verb for ceasing to function goes around everything else

parts.note: a machine that stopped working died

indicators.note: the engineer is held inside the dip

parts.note: a sag is a depression or dip

explanation.surface: An engineer, gripped by depression, quit working outdoors and withdrew from life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low mood but is a physical dip, and 'stopped working' is a machine dying, not someone resigning; the inner wrap gives SENGAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A part that disengaged has come loose from what it was joined to, as gears separating.

clue.text: Approval of god usurped by priest in worship

indicators.note: the god's place is seized by the priest, so one replaces the other

parts.note: adoration is worship
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A god's approval is taken over by a priest during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a proposal is its formal acceptance or approval.

clue.text: Composer's unfinished oratorio with incomplete finale

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the oratorio is left off

parts.note: Messiah is Handel's oratorio

indicators.note: incomplete means the final letter goes

parts.note: an end is a finale

explanation.surface: A composer has left an oratorio unfinished with a missing finale.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivier Messiaen was a 20th-century French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivier Messiaen was a French composer, known for the Quartet for the End of Time.

clue.text: Uproar where French expression of amusement is faced by British

indicators.note: the British letters stand in front, facing the rest

parts.note: ou is French for where
ha-ha expresses laughter

explanation.surface: An uproar over a French laugh at the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is not a link word: OU is French for where.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion, a fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Claim to participate in street dancing

parts.note: to be in is to take part

indicators.note: dancing letters jig around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have joined in the street dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a stake or legal claim in something, such as a share in property.

clue.text: Substantial figure he had invested in former college and not returned

indicators.note: the contracted pronoun-and-verb is placed within the rest

parts.note: a poly, short for polytechnic, was a type of British college that became a university in 1992

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for not is read backwards

parts.note: nor is a word meaning and not
HE'D is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A wealthy figure put money into his old college and never came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NOR into RON; HED is HE'D without its apostrophe. 'Substantial' means solid here, not rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyhedron is a solid geometric shape bounded by flat faces, so a figure with substance in three dimensions.

clue.text: Trouble dogs American behind attack

indicators.note: to dog is to follow closely, so the trouble comes behind

parts.note: ass is American slang for the buttocks
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble hounds an American who is falling behind under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' belongs with American: a US word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack, physically or with criticism.

clue.text: Something of little value hardly raised following objection

indicators.note: the reversed word comes after the objection

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no buts

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: hardly means not, as in hardly the time

explanation.surface: An item worth almost nothing was barely raised after protests.
explanation.definitionFit: A button is a thing of trivial worth, as in not worth a button.

clue.text: Eccentric widower devastated after losing wife

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
the letter for wife is taken away first

explanation.surface: An eccentric widower, devastated after the death of his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing W from WIDOWER leaves six letters that 'devastated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd person, an eccentric.

clue.text: One learning from on-line books by boss

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
E, as in e-mail, means electronic or online
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone learns from e-books supplied by their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not an employer but an ornamental knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone who studies, a person in the process of acquiring knowledge.

clue.text: Greet us with waving action

indicators.note: letters that are waving are shaken about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says hello with a wave of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' goes with a greeting so naturally that it hides its job of shuffling GREET US.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement or deed made to express something, such as a kind action.

clue.text: King George I stops for dying subject?

indicators.note: the numeral stops up the royal cipher, plugging the gap inside it

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's cipher
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: King George I asks about a subject on their deathbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George I' looks like the first King George; the I stands apart as ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed to die, and with King George in the surface, a dying subject of the king.

clue.text: PM behind head of state about following up denial

indicators.note: the word for about comes after the denial, following it up

parts.note: aft means behind, at the back of a ship
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, the British head of state
no is a denial
on means about, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister lags behind the head of state while pursuing a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: PM stands for post meridiem, the hours after midday, the time of day between lunch and evening.

clue.text: Moderate degree partner regularly conceals

indicators.note: the chosen letters hide the degree inside them
taking letters at regular intervals uses every second letter of the word

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A degree that a partner hides from time to time is a modest one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective, but as a verb it means lessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or die down, which is a verb sense of moderate.

clue.text: Lecturer working with fellow author

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A lecturer collaborates with a fellow writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack London was the American author of The Call of the Wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London was an American novelist, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Perform with a man performing as a woman?

definitions.meaning: to ... business is to carry it out or conduct it

definitions.text: a man performing as a woman?
definitions.meaning: read as two words; the question mark flags the play

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to go on stage alongside a drag artiste.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct or carry through a deal, so to perform it; the second sense splits the word whimsically.
